entities.name: Henry III of Virneburg
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Henry III von Virneburg, who died on December 29, 1353, served as a highly contested Archbishop and Elector of Mainz from 1328 until his death, though his effective rule was intermittent and challenged. A scion of the powerful Virneburg noble family from the Eifel region, his tenure epitomized the profound political and ecclesiastical schisms that wracked the Holy Roman Empire in the mid-14th century. His election, occurring amidst the bitter struggle between Emperor Louis IV of Bavaria and the Avignon Papacy, plunged the crucial Prince-Archbishopric of Mainz into a prolonged period of internal conflict and external pressure, making him a central figure in the complex dynamics of imperial-papal relations.

His archiepiscopal career was defined by a protracted schism. Elected by a minority of the Mainz cathedral chapter in 1328, Henry III was a staunch supporter of Emperor Louis IV, who had been excommunicated by Pope John XXII. The Pope refused to confirm Henry, leading to the election of a rival, Baldwin of Luxembourg, Archbishop of Trier, in 1337, and later Gerlach of Nassau in 1346. Despite papal opposition and the presence of anti-archbishops, Henry maintained a significant power base and continued to administer parts of the archdiocese, leveraging imperial support and his family's considerable influence. He actively participated in imperial diets, including the Declaration of Rhense in 1338, which asserted the Emperor's right to rule without papal confirmation, and the Diet of Frankfurt, further solidifying the imperial stance against papal claims.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Henry III's contested archiepiscopacy in Mainz was a microcosm of the larger imperial-papal struggle, directly contributing to the Declaration of Rhense and leaving the vital Archbishopric financially devastated for decades.
